holidays.name: National Popcorn Day
holidays.description: A salute to the fluffy, crunchy snack that powers movie nights everywhere. Pop a batch, then try toppings like cinnamon sugar, parmesan or chili-lime.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial food observance, and its exact origin is unclear. It has become a fixture on American snack calendars.
holidays.funFact: Popcorn kernels pop because of the tiny drop of water sealed inside each one. When it heats to steam, the pressure bursts the hull open.

holidays.name: Tenderness Toward Existence Day
holidays.description: A gentle, offbeat observance that asks people to be kind to every living thing. That includes people, animals, plants and even the bug on your windowsill.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is part of a long tradition of days that encourage compassion.
holidays.funFact: Because it falls on the same day as National Popcorn Day, you could celebrate both by sharing a snack with a friend.

holidays.name: National Tin Can Day
holidays.description: A nostalgic nod to the humble tin can, the invention that put soup, peaches and beans in every pantry. Celebrate by cooking from the cupboard.
holidays.origin: The day is tied to the January 19, 1825 US patent for the tin can, which was granted to Thomas Kensett and Ezra Daggett.
holidays.funFact: Cans existed for decades before the can opener was invented. Early cans were opened with a hammer and chisel.
